title: Positional numerals and zero
summary: Around 500 CE the Indian mathematician Aryabhata devised a positional number system, though it had no zero. In 628 CE Brahmagupta's Brahmasphutasiddhanta became the first text to treat zero as a number in its own right and to discuss its arithmetic. Earlier signs of a placeholder zero appear in the Bakhshali manuscript, which has its own record.

uncertainty.note: Aryabhata finished the Aryabhatiya in 499 CE; Brahmagupta composed the Brahmasphutasiddhanta in 628 CE.

as_recorded.value: In around 500 AD Aryabhata devised a number system which has no zero yet was a positional system
His text, Brahmasphutasiddhanta, The Opening of the Universe, written in 628 CE, is the first to treat zero as a number in its own right and to include a discussion of the arithmetic of zero

where.modern_name: India; stand-in pin at Patna, Bihar

importance.justification: The invention of positional decimal numerals and operational zero transformed arithmetic and algebra worldwide, enabling modern science and global commerce.
